 Below, I look at the latest UFC 333 odds and break down and predict each bout on today's card with updated odds. You can also find my prop and finish projections for each fight.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Let's break it down.
 UFC 333 Predictions
 After examining all betting options, a typical UFC card can offer substantial actionable value, and after looking at the UFC 333 odds, today's event is no exception.
 So, in addition to moneylines and over/unders , I'll break down how I plan to bet on all the fights based on the latest UFC 333 odds, including exact winning methods, winning round props , and whether the match will go to a decision or finish inside the distance.
 Here are my moneyline projections for Saturday:
 And now my prop projections, including odds for the fight to reach a decision, or for each fighter to win by decision, KO/TKO, Submission, or inside the distance (finish).
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement UFC 333 odds are as of Saturday morning and via DraftKings . Bet on UFC 333 with our DraftKings promo code . 
 Picks

 Noah Gugnon vs. Kody Steele

 Fight times are approximate and subject to change. All times are ET.
 Iasmin Lucindo vs. Nicole Caliari
 Nicole Caliari won her strawweight debut in her last outing against Shauna Bannon, following consecutive losses at Flyweight. Still, I think Iasmin Lucindo is the superior grappler in this matchup, and she also has a four-inch reach advantage at distance.
 Lucindo is still young (24), but she hasn't shown the best fight IQ to date, with limited finishing instincts and a tendency to fail to separate from opponents when she has clear advantages.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement As a result, it's hard to lay the juice on her as a substantial favorite; this fight may play out closer than the line suggests, but Lucindo is the better athlete and has more room to progress after a near 15-month layoff.
 And ultimately, I don't project edges on the side, total, or winning method props for this fight.
 Bets 
 Pass
 Noah Gugnon vs. Kody Steele
 I'm close to betting Noah Gugnon in this matchup, but I want a price nearer to +140, compared to my projection at +129. The Frenchman is the better striker in this fight, particularly defensively, and he's a solid grappler too.
 Moreover, Kody Steele tends to get comfortable hunting submissions from bottom, while Gugnon has an excellent top game and nasty ground-and-pound; I could see Steele ceding bad positions and providing subpar minute-winning optics at the wrong moments in this contest.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Steele is a good athlete and should have the cardio edge over most opponents, and he may be the more durable man in this matchup too. Still, I expect Gugnon to land the more damaging strikes in the first 10 minutes and potentially finish it himself.
 While I'd wait for a better number on Gugnon's moneyline, I'm also interested in his odds to win by KO/TKO (projected +358, listed +440) or inside the distance (projected +220, listed +275).
 Alternatively, I also show value on Steele to win by decision (projected +323, listed +440)
 DraftKings is offering the double chance prop for Steele by Decision with Gugnon by KO/TKO at +150; I'd project that fair line at +120.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, if you play both props individually at +440, you can get a higher expected return than the individual +150 double-chance prop.
 I rarely bet on both sides of a fight, but unless you get a better number on Gugnon's moneyline, this seems like the optimal approach; or you can also swap Gugnon inside the distance for his KO line.
 Bets 
 Noah Gugnon wins Inside the Distance (+275, 0.15u), DraftKings; bet to +250
 Kody Steele wins by Decision (+450, 0.1u), FanDuel; bet to +350
 Daniel Santos vs. Bolaji Oki
 Bolaji Oki is the bigger man (3″ taller, 6″ reach), moving down from lightweight for this matchup after consecutive finish losses; cutting additional weight won't improve his durability or cardio.
 As a result, Daniel "Willycat" Santos – who applied pressure, pushes a pace, and should have much better cardio than Oki – is a solid live betting target after five minutes.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Oki is an explosive athlete and should have a power advantage early, and Santos is coming off a knockout loss to Doo Ho Choi in May. Still, Oki tends to put every ounce of power into his efforts, and if he doesn't hurt Santos early, the momentum will eventually slip away.
 I project an edge on Santos to win by KO/TKO (projected +289, listed +350), and I like his odds to win in Round 2 (+750) or 3 (+1200), pre-fight, before firing at his live moneyline.
 Bets 
 Daniel Santos wins by TKO/KO (+360, 0.1u), BallyBet; bet to +350
 Daniel Santos wins in Round 2 (+750, 0.1u), BallyBet; bet to +600
 Daniel Santos wins in Round 3 (+1200, 0.05u), BallyBet; bet to +1000
 Daniel Santos Live after Round 1
 Jacob Malkoun vs. Abubakar Vagaev
 UFC matchmaking has become much more intentional in recent years, and Russian and Chechen regional fighters have often been given soft matchups in Abu Dhabi, accumulating a 33-3 record since 2021, including a 20-1 record in decisions, when they are not facing one another.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement As a result, it's hard to pull the trigger on Jacob Malkoun to win by decision (projected +217, listed +250) in what should be a wrestling match with Abubakar Vagaev; Malkoun has poor finishing instincts, and he's unlikely to get competitive rounds decided in his favor as the away team in this arena.
 While Malkoun can have durability issues, neither man seems powerful enough to threaten the other standing seriously (Vagaev is coming up from welterweight), and both are sound enough defensively to avoid being submitted.
 Still, the price on this fight to go the distance is steep (listed -260) compared to the divisional average of around 59% (-144 implied odds), and I think Malkoun by decision or particularly his point spread (+3.5, -170) are better expressions of that likelihood.
 Bets 
 Jacob Malkoun +3.5 Points (-170, 0.2u), DraftKings; bet to -185
 Colby Thicknesse vs. Asaf Chopurov
 Asaf Chopurov, the UAE Warriors champ, was considered one of the best non-UFC fighters in MMA. Still, he will make his octagon debut on Saturday against Alexander Volkanovski's chief training partner, Colby Thicknesse.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Thicknesse is well-rounded and has never been finished, but he has little finishing power himself; the question is whether he can survive and cover a near 5-1 price tag by surviving against a dangerous debutant.
 Thicknesse came close to falling against both Vince Morales and Josias Musasa in recent wins, and Chopurov – who has just 11 pro fights but 35 amateur MMA bouts under his belt- has a wealth of experience at 24 years old.
 I projected this fight to reach a decision about 45% of the time, compared to a divisional average closer to 54%, and I still see value on the goes-to-decision or distance prop, compared to listed odds of +180.
 Bet Over 2.5 Rounds (+130) or the Fight Goes the Distance Prop (+180) down to +135.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Moreover, I show correlated value on Chopurov to win by decision (projected +195, listed +250) at +225 or better.
 Bets 
 Fight Goes to Decision (+180, 0.2u), FanDuel; bet to +135
 Grant Dawson vs. Nurullo Aliev
 I project an edge on either the Under 2.5 Rounds or Fight to End Inside the Distance, and for Grant Dawson to win by finish (projected +300, listed +360) in Saturday's bout with Nurullo Aliev.
 Dawson is relatively chinny and can be knocked out with a clean shot by any opponent, but he's one of the best back-takers in the sport and offers a lethal rear-naked choke, plus damaging ground-and-pound when opponents let him stay on top.
 Aliev is the younger man (7 years) and a solid wrestler in his own right (11.1 to 5.5 takedown attempts per five minutes at distance in favor of Dawson) who has controlled opponents – in a more limited sample – just as much as Dawson has (90% to 92%). Still, Dawson is the superior finisher if this fight goes to ground.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bet the inside-the-distance prop at +145 or better, and play Dawson to finish to +325.
 Still, in what could be a wrestling-heavy fight, I wouldn't want any part of Dawson's moneyline as the road fighter in Abu Dhabi if it reaches a decision.
 Bets 
 Aliev/Dawson, Fight Ends Inside the Distance (+152, 0.15u), FanDuel; bet to +145.
 Grant Dawson wins Inside the Distance (+360, 0.1u), BetRivers; bet to +325
 Abus Magomedov vs. Cam Rowston
 Abus Magomedov is a fast, dynamic starter with a bad gas tank, and if Cam Rowston can weather the storm for five minutes, I like him to flip the momentum and win in the back half of the fight.
 Magomedov is the quicker man and the superior grappler, and Rowston's takedown defense seems like a potential weakness; still, "The Battle Giraffe" showed he could scramble up consistently against Torrez Finney, and every time he returns to his feet, it should help tire his opponent out. Magomedov doesn't grapple as much as he would if he trusted his cardio.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement I don't project an edge on either side of the pre-fight moneyline. Still, I see a slight edge on Rowston by KO/TKO (projected +373, listed +420), or I would consider his odds to win in Round 2 (+750) or Round 3 (+1400) while awaiting a live opportunity after five minutes on the underdog.
 Bets 
 Cam Rowston wins by TKO/KO (+420, 0.1u), FanDuel; bet to +400
 Cam Rowston wins in Round 2 (+750, 0.1u), Fanatics; bet to +600
 Cam Rowston wins in Round 3 (+1400, 0.05u), Fanatics; bet to +1000
 Cam Rowston Live after Round 1
 Nikita Krylov vs. Abdul Rakhman Yakhyaev
 Abdul Yakhyaev keeps finishing his opposition in Round 1, and he slowed in his lone extended fight; a five-round decision win in 2023. It's hard to tell whether he'll keep fading in longer fights, or whether he's strengthened that part of his skillset.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Yakhyaev is nine years younger than his opponent, Nikita Krylov, who has been knocked out in three of his past four appearances.
 If Krylov survives Round 1, I'd be interested in firing a live bet on the underdog, at odds hopefully double his pre-fight price.
 Still, this spot seems like another potential highlight-reel opportunity for "The Hunter," and I don't mind his odds to win by TKO/KO (projected -130, listed -120) or Round 1 KO/TKO (+175), while awaiting the live entry on Krylov.
 Bets 
 Abdul Yakhyaev wins by KO/TKO in Round 1 (+175, 0.1u), Ballybet; bet to +150
 Nikita Krylov Live after Round 1
 Dominick Reyes vs. Azamat Murzakanov
 Dominick Reyes is the bigger man in this fight – 6″ taller, with a 6″ reach advantage- but he's likely to get sniped by Azamat Murzakanov, a finisher with one-punch power who has consistently defeated longer and taller Light Heavyweights.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Murzkanov is coming off his first career loss and knockout defeat himself- against Paulo Costa in April – and his chin may be cracked now following that performance. He always seemed small for the 205-pound division, and at age 37 he's not getting any younger.
 Still, you have to prefer his durability – Reyes has been knocked out four times, including three KO losses in Round 1. Reyes seemed on his way out of the sport several fights back, but he still has a path to either a knockout win or a volume-based decision as an underdog.
 While my model points to Reyes as the potential value side of this fight, setting his fair odds at +167, compared to odds as high as +186 on prediction markets, I'm still inclined to pass. As stated above, the UFC has been incredibly intentional with their recent matchmaking, and Reyes is the clear "B" side of this matchup.
 Bets 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pass
 Aaron Pico vs. Losene Keita
 Check out my colleague Billy Ward's write-up (link) on Pico-Keita. 
 Aaron Pico is the better martial artist in nearly all his matchups, but he has questionable durability and can be flatlined by high-level opposition.
 Pico should have a clear grappling edge in this fight, but he doesn't always take the path of least resistance, and he doesn't maintain top control as consistently as you'd expect from a wrestler of his caliber.
 Keita's takedown defense hasn't been tested at the UFC level, but regional tape suggests he could get put on his back whenever Pico wants.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, Keita is a dangerous striker, with a size advantage (1″ taller, 2″ reach), and I show a slight edge on his odds to win by finish (projected +235, listed +250) against a talented but chinny opponent.
 Bets 
 TBD
 Alexander Volkov vs. Rizvan Kuniev
 Check out my colleague John LanFranca's write-up (link) on Volkov-Kuniev. 
 Alexander Volkov opened as a bigger favorite in this fight, but the line has moved closer to a pick'em; I projected his moneyline at -126 and would bet him small to -120.
 He's the bigger man (3″ taller, 4″ reach) than Kuniev, with a wealth of fight experience (50+ pro fights), and if Kuniev is unwilling to wrestle, this should be Volkov's fight to lose. Kuniev comes from a Dagestani combat Sambo background, but has seemingly been unwilling to mix takedowns into his game plan since winning on contender series.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Volkov should chip away with straight punches and teeps, and his volume should prove more effective as the fight extends (+2.8 to +0.6 strike differential per minute at distance; 6.3 to 3.7 landed per minute).
 In addition to Volkov's moneyline, I also like this fight to end inside the distance more frequently than the odds suggest (projected +132, listed +160), and for Volkov to potentially find a knockout (projected +383, listed +410) or finish (projected +295, listed +360), but I prefer the simpler approach. I will revisit the violence props before adding them or passing on those.
 Bets 
 Alexander Volkov (-120, 0.25u), Caesars; bet to -120
 Lone'er Kavanagh vs. Ramazan Temirov
 Check out my colleague Billy Ward's write-up (link) on Kavanagh-Temirov. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ramazan Temirov is one of the more aggressive fighters on the roster, marching forward and swinging hooks. Still, he needs to navigate a size discrepancy (2″ shorter, 4″ reach) against Lone'er Kavanagh, who will be the faster man landing combinations from range while staying on his bike.
 Temirov has massive power for Flyweight, with five knockdowns in 22 UFC minutes, and Kavanagh has shown a relatively suspect chin. Temirov can sustain his style for at least ten minutes; all it takes is two big punches that lead to knockdowns, without getting finished, for him to pull the upset.
 Still, Kavanagh's finish losses came against taller, higher-volume strikers in Charles Johnson and Brandon Royval; if this fight gets past Round 1, Kavanagh should start running downhill.
 Temirov would be a bigger problem for Kavanagh in the smaller APEX cage. Still, in the regular-sized octagon, I like the Englishman to navigate space comfortably and find his range.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bet Lone'er live after Round 1, and consider taking a Same Game Parlay (SGP) with Kavanagh and Over 1.5 Rounds (+140) or Kavanagh and Fight Starts Round 2 (+121).
 Bets 
 SGP: Lone'er Kavanagh & Fight Starts Round 2 (+121, 0.1u), Caesars; bet to +110
 Lone'er Kavanagh wins in Round 3 or by Decision (+180, 0.1u), Caesars; bet to +160
 Lone'er Kavanagh Live after Round 1
 Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili
 Check out my colleague Dan Tom's write-up on Saturday's co-main event and bantamweight title bout between Petr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili.
 You can also check out my preview from Yan-Dvalishvili II from December, when I bet Yan on the moneyline and by decision at +350 and +600, respectively.
 With those prices now at -135 and +140, it's hard to get behind the current champion again. However, it's a bit easier to swallow when you recall that Yan was a -240 favorite before the first fight; I think that's closer to the correct line for the trilogy bout.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Yan was severely compromised during the first fight, throwing his right hand fewer than five times across a 25-minute bout. Moreover, that fight being in the APEX benefitted Merab greatly, as he could consistently pursue takedown attempts and shove Yan up against the fence while giving the Russian limited opportunities to get back to the center of the cage.
 Yan is one of the best anti-wrestlers in the sport – perhaps the best now that Jose Aldo has retired – and he has shown an ability to mix in trip takedowns against both Merab and his teammate, Aljamain Sterling, in their four prior encounters. His style seems like the perfect antidote to Merab's aggression, and I don't think "The Machine" can get back to his peak self at 35; his best efforts are likely behind him.
 Prime Merab is unlike anything I have ever seen, but I do think his athleticism has crested. He doesn't have a fighting style that will age particularly well, as his physicality continues to diminish.
 Merab landed more significant strikes than Yan in the rematch. Still, he absorbed much more damage than his opponent, and if the trend continues, Yan could become the second man to finish Dvalishvili in MMA and the first to knock him out.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement I project an edge on Yan's moneyline, and would bet him up to -165 (projected -180). However, I don't see an edge on the total or any winning-method props.
 Yan also typically starts slowly to make his reads before stepping on the gas in Round 2; he's worth a live bet after Round 1 if he falls behind in any matchup.
 Bets 
 Petr Yan (-135, 0.5u), DraftKings; bet to -165
 Petr Yan Live after Round 1
 Alexander Volkanovski vs. Movsar Evloev
 For more information, including a full statistical breakdown of Saturday's main event, check out my full fight preview .
 In short, I projected Evloev as a 54.5% favorite (-120 implied odds) in this fight, and I would play his moneyline up to -110.
 However, I prefer his finish props, projecting Evloev to win by TKO/KO at +782 and his inside-the-distance prop at +476, compared to listed odds of +1000 and +600; bet Evloev to record his first UFC knockout and/or finish at +850 and +500, respectively.
 To that end, I also like Evloev in the finish-only market at even money or better.
 And lastly, you can find Evloev to land 1+ knockdown at +480 at FanDuel (albeit at small limits); take that prop down to +400.
 Evloev has been extremely unlucky not to get a finish during his UFC run, facing a litany of durable opponents; However, he hasn't recorded an official knockdown. He has wobbled and bloodied several of his foes. And while Volkanovski is the most skilled opponent he's faced, he's also one of the less durable opponents Evloev has drawn over this 11-fight run.
 Bets 
 Movsar Evloev (+104, 0.25u), NoVig; bet to -110
